# Proud Project / Conflict / Failure

[← Snowflake](../README.md) · [Every Snowflake question](../../snowflake.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/onsite-behavioral-proud-conflict-failure)

`conflict` `ownership`

---

## Requirements

- Have a story ready about the project you are proudest of.
- Prepare an example involving conflict or disagreement.
- Prepare an account of a failure.
- Every response should explain your role, the specific technical or product stakes, what you did yourself, and the result.

## Notes

- These questions often accompany a mid-level onsite that includes a coding round and a system-design round. The behavioral round is substantive rather than ceremonial and may influence the final-loop decision.
- Make the proud-project story technical enough to support follow-up questions. Interviewers may use it to examine scope, ownership, and how you worked through trade-offs.
- Conflict and failure responses should finish by describing a behavior that changed, not merely an incident that was resolved.

## Preparation

- Write one STAR-based proud-project story that includes metrics and a technical trade-off.
- Prepare a conflict story in which the disagreement concerned substance rather than interpersonal friction.
- Prepare a failure story in which you accept responsibility for the miss and can identify the process or engineering change that resulted.
